terra.problem: Papa's family is his six cookie cutter kids, not the batteries in the drawer.
“The wrong end of the family tree” calls the baker's answer wrong.
The palace comes up before Joash is seated on the throne, in 2 Chronicles 23:5 and 23:15.
The passage does not call Jehoiada's plan secret.
Verse 8 does not say that each commander took his men. It says the Levites and all Judah did as Jehoiada ordered, and each took his men.
Verse 8 does not say each commander took both groups. It also describes men coming on and going off duty, though Jehoiada had not released any divisions, so “no shift change” is misleading.
The cited verse identifies Saul as king, but does not establish that he was Israel's first king.
The verse says Jehoiada and his sons anointed Joash and shouted, not that the crowd shouted. “One minute” and “the next” also compress the six years Joash was hidden.
The explanation calls an ephod a priest's garment without a reference for that fact from outside the passage.
The passage does not say the crowning and covenant happened on the same day.
The explanation repeats the covenant's participants without adding a useful explanation or Papa's personality.
The passage says the people tore down Baal's temple and smashed its altars and idols. It does not say they took apart everything associated with Baal.
“When the text says tore down, it means tore down” repeats the answer without adding explanation or personality.
Saying the priests were “back” at the job implies they had previously stopped doing it, which this passage does not say.
“A little while before” adds a time interval the passage does not give.
The people rejoiced and the city was quiet, but the text does not say nobody in the city was frightened.
